department: Finance (OpenAlex/INFORMS topic: Corporate Finance and Governance; manuscript ID MS-FIN-2023-04231; accepted by Bo Becker, finance)
title: Corporate Acquisitions and Bank Relationships
authors: Steven Poelhekke; Razvan Vlahu; Vadym Volosovych
near_miss_reason: Not coded as a near miss because removing the time-varying controls would still not leave a TWFE regression. Every reported column is a long-difference regression (outcome = bank-relationship measure at t+1 minus t-1) with NO firm fixed effects, with lagged-outcome-level fixed effects (absorb(l1_bankrelationships_f l1_bankrelationships_d)), with eight lagged time-varying financial controls ($fincontrol), with the sample truncated at the acquisition year (l1_adi50a==0, so each acquired firm contributes a single treated observation and no later post-periods), and in most columns with CEM matching weights. Tables 3-6 additionally add heterogeneity treatment regressors; Tables 7 and 9 compare foreign vs domestic acquisitions among acquired firms only. The deviations are structural (estimator and sample), not just controls.
eligible_reason: The underlying treatment qualifies structurally: a majority acquisition (a shareholder moves from <10% or absent to >50%, or from 10-50% to >50%) is a binary absorbing event (adi50a = 1 from the acquisition year onward, replace adi50a=l.adi50a if l.adi50a==1) occurring at firm-specific years within a 2008-2014 firm-bank panel for 23 European countries, with never-acquired firms as controls. But no reported specification is a levels regression with unit and calendar-time fixed effects. All regressions in Section 3D of the replication instructions take the form reghdfe d1Y addi50a $fincontrol [$controls] if afdi50a==0 & resold!=1 & l1_adi50a==0 [aweight=cem_weights_treat_dom_matched*], absorb(sectoryear l1_bankrelationships_f l1_bankrelationships_d) cluster(countrysectoryear), where d1Y = f.Y - l.Y (change from t-1 to t+1). This is a first-difference/event-year design without firm FE, with lagged outcome levels as FE (protocol excludes lagged outcomes), eight time-varying lagged financial controls in every column, post-acquisition years beyond t=0 dropped, and CEM reweighting (matching-based) in the headline matched columns. Hence eligible = false while eligible_design = true.
design_notes: Firm-year panel built from Orbis/Amadeus (KSVVY harmonized financials and ownership, 2000-2014) merged with Orbis Bank Focus/Amadeus 'banker' fields (firm-bank relationships, annual vintages 2010-2015 covering 2008-2014). Treatment construction (Section 3A, PDF p. 20-21): fdi50/ddi50 = new foreign/domestic >50% owner whose lagged stake was <10% or missing; efdi50/eddi50 = existing 10-50% owner moving above 50%; adi50 = any of the four; adi50a = absorbing version; afdi50a = absorbing foreign acquisition; addi50a (used in the regressions) is the absorbing domestic-acquisition indicator by the same naming convention (addi50 appears in the heterogeneity loop at PDF-text line 979 but its gen line is not shown). Outcomes: d1bankrelationships = bankrelationships(t+1) - bankrelationships(t-1) (Section C.5, 'Change in the number of bank relationships (t-1 to t+1)'), f1addbank_l2_sum and f1dropbank2_l2_sum (banks added/dropped t-1 to t+1), d1ihsmeanbr_assets_* (change in asinh of mean bank client assets in target's country/region/NUTS1/NUTS2/city), d1ihsmeanbank_ccitiespres (cities served), d1bankssec*_specpara2_q34 (sector-specialized banks). Estimation: reghdfe with sectoryear FE (NACE Rev.2 core code x year) plus FE for lagged number of foreign and domestic bank relationships; cluster countrysectoryear; sample afdi50a==0 (domestic acquisitions only) & resold!=1 (never resold) & l1_adi50a==0 (not already acquired last year). Unmatched columns add samebank_preacquisition; matched columns use CEM weights (Matched 1: l1_OPER_TURN, l1_empl, growth and size covariates within country x NACE2 x year cells; Matched 2 adds l1_leverage2; Matched 3 adds lagged domestic/foreign bank counts and samebank_preacquisition as exact-match binaries). The README's prose (Section 3A) says 'First-difference/DID logic with firm fixed effects, sector x year fixed effects, time trends', but no absorb() in the code includes a firm identifier or trends. No event-study or dynamic specification appears; the l1_adi50a==0 restriction removes all post-acquisition observations after the acquisition year, so no dynamic version can be built from the reported sample.
estimators_reported: first_difference_did (long difference t-1 to t+1) with sector-year FE and lagged-outcome-level FE, time-varying controls
cem_matched_weighted_regression (same specification with aweight = CEM weights)
heterogeneity_interactions (addi50a x different NUTS2 region / different NACE sector)
treated_only_comparison (foreign vs domestic acquisition among acquired firms, Tables 7 and 9)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Not recoverable from the package (no analysis data). Acquisition years are firm-specific within a 2008-2014 firm-bank panel; events require a lagged ownership observation and the outcome requires a t+1 lead, so at most 5-6 acquisition-year cohorts (approx. 2009-2013/2014) plus never-acquired firms.
modern_estimator_note: No csdid, did_imputation, eventstudyinteract, did_multiplegt or did2s call appears in the package code excerpts. The full-text search flags for this article (ft_de_chaisemartin, ft_sun_and_abraham, ft_staggered) indicate the published text cites de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille and Sun-Abraham, possibly as a discussion or an appendix robustness check that is not part of the package; re-check when the article text is available.

Inputs are Moody's/Bureau van Dijk Orbis (financials, identifiers, sectors), Orbis Ownership, Orbis Bank Focus (legacy Bankscope) and Amadeus banker fields, plus the KSVVY harmonized Orbis panel (Kalemli-Ozcan et al. 2024). Only two single-firm example files with disguised IDs are shipped.

screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Design inferred from the Stata excerpts in the replication-instructions PDF, Sections 3A (treatment construction), 3B (CEM), C.5 (outcome transformations: d1Y = f.Y - l.Y) and 3D (Tables 1-9). Treatment variable in regressions is addi50a (absorbing domestic acquisition); its gen line is not in the excerpt but adi50a/afdi50a are defined as absorbing at PDF p. 21, and addi50 appears in the heterogeneity loop at pdftotext line 979. The README prose claims firm fixed effects and time trends, but none of the transcribed absorb() lists includes a firm identifier or trend. If the published article contains an appendix with a levels TWFE or a Sun-Abraham / de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille robustness check (suggested by the full-text flags), that would need to be screened from the text; the package gives no code for it.
